# Per-workload model roles inventory

Status: **Implemented locally on `harsha/model-roles`; no push.**
Persistence approval: Harsha, 2026-09-24 Slack DM, as supplied in the task:
optional `modelRoles` map on existing AW-Organizations records; no new table/index.
Author: `deploy <deploy@agentweb.pro>`.

## Implemented contract

Eight roles live in `backend/src/services/modelRoles.ts`. The resolver uses the
organization override when it is selectable, otherwise the validated default.
Options come from the text and extracted image registries, excluding restricted,
static-legacy and dominance-derived legacy models. Text roles exclude Live models;
chat/research require tools; voice requires the existing Live transport capability.
The image preview alias is excluded from new selections. A role's own default is always
selectable, even when dominance would hide it as superseded (ENG-2720: `gpt-5.6-luna`), so an
org can save it and an override of it does not resolve to its successor.

| Role | Default source, then validated fallback |
| --- | --- |
| chat | `agent_mode_default_model`, then `gemini-3.8-flash` |
| enrichment | `openrouter/openai/gpt-5.6-luna` (ENG-2720; was `gpt-5.5`, itself what enrichment ran before model roles). `CRM_ENRICH_V3_DEFAULT_MODEL` overrides it on the environment, so a rollback needs no code deploy. ENG-2184: the flash-lite default silently moved prod enrichment to a model at 1/20 the price and quality index 16 vs 38; Luna was benchmarked on a real 112-lead list at about 99% of the fields filled and about 5% of the LLM cost, with somewhat weaker web-value sourcing (ENG-2720). |
| image | `agent_mode_image_api_default_model`, then older `default_image_model` when absent, then `gemini-3-pro-image-preview` |
| embedding | `openai/text-embedding-3-large` via the shared OpenRouter embeddings helper; 1536 output dimensions |
| scoring_judge | `default-scoring-model`, then `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` |
| content_generation | `agent_mode_content_model`, then `gemini-3.8-flash` |
| research | `gemini-3.8-flash` (tool-capable text; specialized Sonar adapter remains separate) |
| voice | `gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview` |

Embedding options deliberately contain only the existing OpenRouter model. Two models
with 1536 output dimensions can still have incompatible vector spaces; adding a
second model needs a separately approved reindex/migration. The shared helper
requests 1536 dimensions and rejects malformed/non-finite/wrong-size vectors.

`harsha/model-supersession` is not an ancestor of this branch and its module is
absent. Invalid and legacy overrides therefore use the default, as requested;
after that branch merges, successor resolution is a follow-up and must still
pass the role capability filter.

Organization overrides and user-to-org membership have bounded 15-second caches
(maximum 1000 entries each). Membership caching is only for model preferences,
never authorization. A successful PUT invalidates the local org cache; other
processes converge after TTL. Runtime storage-read failures use validated defaults
and are not cached; API persistence failures return errors.

## API

Authenticated org owners/admins only, for both methods:
`GET/PUT /api/orgs/me/model-roles`. Org identity and role are loaded from the
authenticated user; a supplied org ID has no authority.

GET returns `{ modelRoles, revision, roles }`; each role includes `defaultModel`,
`effectiveModel`, and `allowedModels`. PUT takes `{ modelRoles, revision }` and
replaces the map. Omitted roles reset to defaults; `{}` resets all. Use the GET
revision (string or null). Unknown roles, non-string values, wrong capabilities,
restricted and legacy models are rejected. Missing revision: 428; stale revision:
409; storage failure: 500. The atomic DynamoDB update touches only `modelRoles`
and `updatedAt`, requires the org to still exist, and advances the revision even
when the clock has not advanced.

The org-settings frontend lives in **agentweb-customer-portal**, not this repo.
The in-repo partner portal has platform-admin settings, not org settings. Add the
Models section with eight pickers in the customer-portal follow-up, using this API.

## Migrated runtime sites

- Enrichment V3: non-web extraction, identity candidate disambiguation, LinkedIn
  candidate selection, smart-field evaluation, the web-search tier and the critic
  (ENG-2184), so one run uses one model. ENG-2720: OpenAI-model web-search calls skip Azure (it errors on the
  search tool), and calls on the default Luna model retry on `gpt-5.5` if OpenRouter reports a provider
  failure; that fallback does not cover a 200 response with an empty body. Smart-field attribution records the
  resolved model. The `CRM_ENRICH_V3_*` env overrides still take precedence.
- Image: both agent-mode's upstream default and the shared image generator.
  Explicit request models and existing retry/fallback semantics are preserved.
- Embedding: shared `embedText` (memory/relevance and its callers), via user tenant.
- Judges: default session scoring and custom judges with no explicit model.
  Explicit custom-judge/benchmark models retain their existing validation path.
- Content: blog generation, blog restyling (tenant propagated from agent mode and
  the HTTP controller), report revision and social engagement memory generation.

## Remaining follow-ups

- Customer-portal Models UI (separate repository).
- Chat/session/scheduled-chat defaults, with explicit session/user choices first.
- Specialized research/Sonar, live voice transport and voice artifact extraction.
- Older enrichment extraction/mapping paths.
- Knowledge-base embeddings inside `chatbotService.findRelevantChunks` (currently
  no tenant context), plus other direct SDK/vector ingestion paths. Propagate
  tenant/index identity before migration; no alternate embedding space enabled.
- Remaining report/workflow/content callers, classification/summary helpers,
  confirmation/stop/step-removal judges, system cron jobs, scripts and benchmarks.
- Successor integration after model-supersession merges.

The lexical inventory below is a historical snapshot, not a count of runtime
migrations or traffic measurements. Literal registry/pricing/provider translation
IDs and historical telemetry are not replacement targets.

## Validation, rollout and complexity

**153 tests passed across 9 focused Jest suites.** Coverage includes
override/default/legacy/capability behavior, tenant isolation,
TTL, admin authorization, malformed inputs, stale-write rejection, deleted-org
protection, reset, storage failures, embedding shape, judge precedence and image
routing. Existing focused embedding, scoring, org-write and image suites are run.
Jest reported open handles: a focused `--detectOpenHandles` run traced these to
the existing image `withTimeout` implementation, which leaves timeout timers
alive after a successful race. This is a separate cleanup follow-up; assertions
pass, but the worker requires forced shutdown.

A bounded 1 GB `tsc --noEmit` checks the new resolver/API/registry/classification
modules and source-extracted org read/write methods against narrow source-derived
contracts. Changed integration files receive syntax/transpile checks. This is
**not** a full backend build: checking their full transitive graph exhausted 1.5 GB
and 3 GB heaps. Full production build and before/after provider/Okareo parity are
still required before any later shipping step; no push/deploy is part of this task.

Local CodeRabbit completed its initial review with three overlapping findings
about repeated membership reads and settings/org/user read outages; all were
addressed. This is not a latest-diff clean verdict; the final fixes were checked
with the scoped tests and bounded TypeScript check. No production settings/data were read or mutated.
Linear search was retried but the connector requires reauthentication, so no issue
could be created/claimed. The user's explicit task is the acceptance contract.

Complexity: one role resolver, one org map/API, shared image IDs and extracted
existing model-classification helpers; no new provider adapter, dependency, table
or index. Replaces scattered defaults. The original classification exports remain
available from agentModeService for compatibility. Rollback: revert code; the
optional map is ignored by old code. Reset through PUT restores role defaults.

## Exhaustive lexical evidence

The table includes source snippets so both literal model IDs and dynamic selection
expressions are visible. Proposed roles and purposes are conservative triage based
on the file/line context, not proof a line is an executable LLM call. Includes
comments, documentation, registry/pricing entries, model propagation and attribution
on purpose: these are distinguished from migration targets in the purpose column.
Non-test source only; excludes test/spec files, test scripts, test/mock/fixture
directories. Multi-line calls are represented by their model-bearing lines.

Search: case-insensitive identifiers containing `model`, plus GPT/Gemini/Claude,
text-embedding, Sonar, gen4_image, DALL-E and other provider/model-family literals
(DeepSeek, Qwen, Grok, Mistral, Llama, Kimi, o-series, Nova, Imagen, Veo,
Whisper, TTS, Flux, Command-R and GLM). Executed over tracked/
unignored source paths enumerated by `rg --files backend/src`; no dependency or
build-output directories were scanned. All matched lines are retained without
truncation. This broad search also captures unrelated business/data-model mentions;
those are evidence to discard during migration, not instructions to change them.

Found **4747 matching lines in 314 non-test files**.

| backend/src/emma/tools.ts:5345 | <code>description: 'Generate or edit images using AI image generation models. Supports both text-to-image generation and image editing with input images.\n\nMULTIPLE VARIANTS: When the user asks for several INDEPENDENT variants of the same brief (e.g. "generate 3 variants"), emit ALL the generate_image calls together in a SINGLE turn — one tool call per variant. They run in parallel (bounded), so N variants finish in roughly the time of one instead of N× and stay within the turn\'s time limit; generating them one-by-one across separate turns is slow and can time out. Only chain image calls sequentially when a later image genuinely DEPENDS on an earlier one (e.g. editing a just-generated image).\n\nLOGO COMPOSITING BEST PRACTICES (tested and confirmed):\n- When the user wants an image with their logo, ALWAYS use the logo_image parameter with the logo URL from their brand guidelines (read_brand_guidelines tool). Do NOT describe the logo in the prompt — pass the actual PNG URL.\n- For logo compositing, prefer gemini-3.1-flash-image or gemini-3-pro-image-preview. Both successfully composite PNG logos with high fidelity. gemini-3.1-flash-image renders the logo largest and most prominently. These models also produce 4096×4096 output.\n- gpt-image-2 also supports logo compositing via logo_image and works correctly, preserving the logo faithfully at 1024×1024 (may add unrequested design elements around it).\n- gpt-image-1 is NOT reliable for logo compositing — it rewrites the logo (e.g. replaces the actual text in the logo with the company name from the prompt). Avoid gpt-image-1 when logo fidelity matters.\n- NEVER tell the user that AI image generation cannot composite a real logo — gemini-3-pro-image-preview, gemini-3.1-flash-image, and gpt-image-2 all handle it correctly when logo_image is provided.\n- NEVER switch the output format from image to HTML without explicit user approval.\n- Brand guideline PNG logos from the attachments array composite cleanly — use them directly.\n\nTRANSPARENT BACKGROUNDS — DO NOT use generate_image to "redraw the logo on a transparent background". This model redraws the mark and can drift its icon/letters/colors, and it CANNOT guarantee a true alpha channel. To make an existing logo\'s background transparent, use the remove_image_background tool (it operates on the original pixels and outputs genuine alpha). If the user already has a transparent PNG of the logo, use that directly. Only fall back to generation if no source logo exists at all.\n\nTEXT &amp; DATA RELIABILITY (known model limitation — brief around it, do NOT retry expecting a better roll):\n- Image models cannot reliably render small exact text — specific IDs/codes, short spelled-out strings, or any string that must match character-for-character (e.g. "campaign 120214893"). At small sizes the model commonly repeats a garbled or truncated approximation of the string in every occurrence instead of the real value. Do NOT ask for an exact short identifier to appear (especially more than once) and do NOT retry the same prompt hoping the string comes out right next time — it won\'t reliably. Instead brief around it: use a generic/illustrative label ("Campaign A"), keep any exact identifier out of the image and reference it in the surrounding chat text instead, or enlarge it to be the sole hero text of the image rather than one of several small repeated labels.\n- When a prompt asks for a data-shaped layout (a table, chart, or list of metrics), the model tends to invent plausible-looking numbers/data for cells it doesn\'t actually have values for, rather than leaving them blank. NEVER ask generate_image to fill in real metrics or figures you don\'t already have from a tool result — either pass the exact real values in the prompt, or explicitly instruct the prompt to leave those cells blank or empty. Never present the resulting image\'s invented numbers to the user as real data.\n- This also applies when the USER never asked for real data at all. A prompt that merely describes dashboard-like UI elements (a "metrics preview" panel, KPI cards, a progress/stat block, a completion/progress-bar PERCENTAGE) without specifying values will still get invented numbers filled in — the model treats an unstated metric as one it should make up, not one to leave blank. Whenever your own generate_image prompt includes any such element, explicitly state placeholder values ("--", empty, or a generic status word) for it, exactly as you would for an explicit data-table request. Do not assume omitting a value is enough to keep it blank — and do NOT write a specific-looking number into the prompt yourself as a design flourish (e.g. "progress bar at 75%") unless it came from a real tool result. A plausible percentage you invented while writing the prompt is exactly the fabricated data this rule exists to prevent, even though nothing about generating it looks broken.\n- A data-shaped prompt is automatically re-checked against the actual generated image unless you set metrics_verified=true — only do that when every value in the prompt is genuinely sourced from a real tool result this turn, since it skips the check.',</code> | tools — model selection, routing, configuration or attribution | image |
